releases.headline: Fighting changes the farm, and farming changes where fights happen.

World Ecology: The arena now runs a 4×4 grid of sixteen invisible ecological sectors tracking maturity, pressure, real neutral XP value, recent harvesting, combat disturbance, and physical migration flow.
Quiet sectors mature into richer farming geography while heavily harvested or fought-over ground becomes temporarily poorer and recovers over time.
A shared match-age maturity ceiling keeps the richest neutral concentrations from appearing immediately and lets the world support higher-value farming later in a run.
The canonical 62 / 30 / 16 / 8 / 4 Circle/Triangle/Square/Pentagon/Hexagon population contract remains unchanged: Living Front rearranges value instead of simply adding more entities.
There are no hidden XP-zone multipliers and no player-relative pity logic. Valuable ground is valuable because valuable neutral shapes physically exist there.
Neutral Shape Behaviors: Circles remain reliable basic fodder, but now loosely school and gently drift away from visible local danger instead of behaving like completely static XP rocks.

Triangles can make one readable, cooldown-bounded lateral evade when a credible visible projectile threatens them. They cannot chain perfect dodges, so leading, baiting, and follow-up placement are rewarded.
Squares intentionally remain simple, stable farming targets and resist disturbance much more strongly than Circles or Triangles.
Pentagon and Hexagon deaths preserve their split cascades, with child momentum influenced by the final impact geometry so pre-kill positioning can make cleanup easier or harder.
Hexagons are now ecological keystones: an undisturbed Hexagon weakly gathers nearby lower-value shapes into a loose, terrain-visible pocket instead of acting as a global magnet.
Shape instincts respect Battlefield terrain and line of sight, so schooling, attraction, threat response, and local disturbance do not operate magically through walls.
Crashers and Rogue Stars: Crashers have been rebuilt as readable predators using the full Track → Telegraph → Charge → Overshoot → Recover attack grammar.
A committed Crasher charge mostly locks its bearing, can collide with real terrain, carries through a miss into an explicit overshoot, and exposes a recovery window before it can attack again.
Crashers can prey on neutral shapes and store part of that lost value as capped bounty. A brighter core means more reward when destroyed — never extra HP, damage, or speed.

Rogue Stars are now fast roaming prizes rather than slow mini-bosses. Their cruise speed is tuned to outrun ordinary unbuffed tanks, making route prediction and interception stronger than simply tail-chasing them.
Stars use readable long-form movement, respect terrain, remain killable with normal combat tools, and do not gain boss phases or special combat stats.
Disturbance, Herding and Migration: Gunfire, explosions, tank presence, damage, deaths, and rapid harvesting now feed local ecological pressure instead of disappearing from the arena economy the moment combat ends.

Nearby visible fire and blast disturbance can physically herd susceptible Circles and Triangles. Squares resist strongly, Pentagons resist almost entirely, and Hexagons, Stars, and Crashers do not become player-controlled herding units.
Per-shape disturbance memory creates diminishing response, preventing repeated empty firing from becoming the optimal way to farm.

When one area stays hot and nearby ground is calmer, neutral populations can bias movement toward the calmer region. Migration is physical, terrain-constrained movement — never teleportation between sectors.
Because combat can scatter or redirect farm, winning a fight can change the value and traffic of the surrounding battlefield after the fight is over.
Front Director: BLOOM announces a naturally matured high-value pocket that already exists. The Director does not spawn the value or add an XP multiplier when it calls a Bloom.
MIGRATION is announced only after enough real neutral entities have physically crossed sector boundaries in a coherent direction.
ROGUE STAR is the one deliberately created Director opportunity: after a sufficiently quiet stretch, a single fast Star may enter as a globally readable interception prize.
Director opportunities use cooldowns and existing-state gates to prevent event spam, duplicate Stars, or constant forced objectives.
Signals are deliberately restrained: short world/minimap/audio communication instead of capture bars, permanent ecology HUDs, quest trackers, or new controls.
Living Front remains fully active with the Front Director disabled; the Director is a referee/commentator for an already-living world, not the source of the gameplay.
AI and Class Integration: AI can value Blooms, Migrations, Rogue Stars, and locally visible neutral concentrations as strategic opportunities, but ecology remains one utility among combat, survival, routing, and role priorities.
AI receives public Director signals plus Fair Engagement-legal visible ecology only. Hidden sector maturity and unseen neutral positions are not exposed as omniscient data.
Route cost, current health, active fight pressure, deterministic damping, and opportunity saturation keep every bot from rotating to the same ecological hotspot at once.
Controller drones remain strong local autonomous farmers, but they do not independently abandon the player to chase distant Blooms, Stars, or other macro objectives.

No class receives a bespoke ecology stat bonus. Gunner, Cannon, Guardian, Sniper, and Controller interact with Living Front through the combat, terrain, range, splash, mobility, and drone tools they already own.
Progression and Skill: Living Front adds a skill layer to farming through reading mature ground, rotating efficiently, positioning before cascades, predicting Star routes, judging contested value, and exploiting terrain without adding another resource or combo meter.
Ordinary nearby farming remains viable; ecological mastery is intended to improve efficiency rather than make the old play style nonfunctional.

Later-match world maturity supports richer physical farming opportunities as progression costs rise, but the same mature world is available to everyone and never checks whether a particular player is behind.
The system deliberately avoids pity rewards, hidden catch-up multipliers, capture-zone bonuses, crafting currency, faction territory, quest objectives, or ecology skill trees.
Readability, Tips and Debugging: Crasher charge preparation, overshoot residue, fed-core brightness, Rogue Star motion, and short Director signals expose important state without adding permanent screen clutter.

Seven tactical Living Front tips were added through the canonical Fieldcraft registry, covering quiet-ground maturity, Hexagon pockets, Triangle baiting, Crasher bounty, Bloom choices, Star interception, and bounded herding.
Living Front visuals declare Signal Discipline intent so effects stay tied to navigation, threat reading, or actionable battlefield state instead of decorative noise.

Debug now exposes copyable ecological telemetry including all sixteen sectors, maturity/pressure, available neutral XP, migration, shape counts, Triangle evasions, Crasher charge outcomes, bounty flow, Stars, Blooms, AI rotations, planning cost, and player neutral XP/min.
Neutral farming telemetry distinguishes shape/bounty XP from PvP tank-drop orbs so progression tuning is based on the correct reward source.
Performance, Fairness and Reliability: Ecology planning is decimated instead of running every frame: sectors update at roughly 4–5 Hz, shape intent around 8–10 Hz, the Director around 1–2 Hz, and strategic AI ecology at a similarly bounded cadence while movement/collision remain frame-exact.

Living Front reuses NOVA's canonical spatial hash and adds one reusable local projectile index per behavior tick so Triangle threat reading and near-fire herding stay projectile-aware without shape×all-projectile scans.
The release preserves bounded entity counts and favors smarter arrangement over spawning more neutral objects.
A cross-system Crasher fix now expires Battlefield's terrain-bump marker correctly so hitting a wall cancels the current committed charge without poisoning every future charge.
Living Front shipped after an adversarial completion audit corrected twelve concrete gameplay, optimized-runtime, fairness, telemetry, ownership, and governance defects.
The production chain validates Ecology Core → Wild Instincts → Front Director after v1.11.2 Fair Engagement before game boot.

releases.headline: Enemy intelligence follows the same battlefield information language the player can reason about.

Fair Information: Enemy hull perception follows the gameplay viewport and camera projection instead of an arbitrary privileged vision radius.
Forward Observer relay remains the deliberate off-viewport exception while physical line-of-sight still governs firing and terrain interactions.
Target scoring is identity-neutral and does not prioritize a tank merely because it is the human player.
Engagement Discipline: Soft saturation spreads equivalent fights without forbidding legitimate gangs.
Legacy AI receives only the fairly selected perceived rival and bounded reaction cadence remains authoritative.
Controller held-aim repair preserves the two-stick contract without fabricating a released command.

releases.headline: Authorized owner task state reaches NOVA without becoming public gameplay authority.

Owner Surface: The private owner HUD is loaded through pwa-register.js rather than the combat patch chain.
Owner operations fail closed unless the authorized phone bridge is present and events match the active phone binding.
The queue covers supported task/agent states while remaining separate from normal public gameplay.
Companion: The Android NOVA Owner companion is compiled in CI and preserves explicit authorization rather than browser fingerprint identity.

releases.headline: Portrait Blackglass gets a properly proportioned simulator and collision-free guidance.

Blackglass Fit: Portrait Blackglass keeps the v1.7.2 single-column containment but replaces the fixed-height simulator with a responsive 4:3 display bay.
The mobile steering hint moves to a compact top-corner chip and reads DRAG TO STEER, separating it from the canvas-drawn LIVE CHASSIS SIMULATION footer.
Very narrow phones receive a slightly taller display ratio so the chassis stays visually spacious without reintroducing horizontal overflow.
Validation: Added regression coverage for responsive simulator geometry, non-overlapping touch guidance, and stylesheet ordering after the containment layer.

releases.headline: The new disciplines learn to fight the battlefield instead of merely colliding with it.

Battlefield Intelligence: AI tanks use predictive short-horizon terrain probes and local corner waypoints to route around nearby fortifications before grinding into them.
AI may investigate the last position where it legitimately saw a target for a short time, but hidden target movement is never updated until real reacquisition.
Controller drones reuse local corner routing while forming, farming, defending and recalling; locked attack dives remain committed and crash into cover instead of cheating around it.
Cannon AI can intentionally fire on destructible cover blocking a recent legitimate contact, turning breaching into a real tactical choice rather than through-wall pressure.
Cover and Explosions: Hard cover now occludes blast damage as well as bullets and sight.
Partial exposure around an edge is sampled across the target hull, so peeking out of cover can receive partial blast damage without explosions applying full damage through solid walls.
Countercharged Guardian shots gain modest structural authority, letting a successful read convert into limited map pressure without replacing Cannon as the dedicated breaching lineage.
Three Disciplines × Battlefield: The Cannon fuse display now distinguishes the programmed FUSE point from an earlier physical IMPACT against terrain.
Blocked fuse paths identify actual collision distance and remaining destructible-cover integrity instead of pretending the programmed airburst is reachable.
Apex Cannon structural specialization continues to flow through Battlefield's canonical break, rubble, score and feedback systems.
Blackglass Containment: Fixed the real portrait-mobile showroom regression where the late-injected base stylesheet could override the earlier mobile polish and restore the three-column desktop grid.
Portrait/coarse-pointer devices now receive an explicit bounded single-column showroom: dossier rail, animated stage, identity, telemetry and graft lab all remain inside the phone viewport.
Hard min-width/max-width/overflow rules prevent intelligence text, stat values, graft deltas and library cards from leaking beyond the screen or drawing over adjacent sections.
The containment stylesheet reasserts itself after the base showroom stylesheet appears, making the fix resilient to DOMContentLoaded load order.
Validation: Added regression tests for blast occlusion, partial exposure, local waypoint routing, Cannon impact preview, intentional structural fire and legitimate last-seen AI memory.
The production materializer syntax-checks every runtime layer and now loads Combined Arms plus the Blackglass containment layer after Apex Doctrine.

releases.headline: Apex tanks stop being bigger parents and become distinct mastery problems.

Gunner Apex Doctrine: Tempest gains a broad redline cadence band with top sustained throughput, but overshooting it adds severe recoil and recovery.
Needle Storm gains a narrow precision gate where exact heat plus stable tracking accelerates, strengthens, and hardens needles.
Breachlord rewards a settled cooled brace volley, then exposes a short movement-recovery punish window.
Flakmaster turns stability into tighter, faster, longer-lived pellets for deliberate ranged shotgun play.
Cannon Apex Doctrine: Cluster King fuse depth now controls child-bomb sector width as well as detonation distance: short programs spread wide, deep programs focus forward.
Siege Bomber's structural specialization now actually converts into extra destructible-cover damage while Battlefield keeps ownership of breach and rubble feedback.
Annihilator gains stronger deep-fuse blast commitment at the cost of a larger reload opening.
Quake Cannon converts deeper fuse programs into stronger displacement and wider shock geometry rather than raw damage inflation.
Guardian Apex Doctrine: Bastion can anchor nearly stationary for extra frontal lane efficiency; moving or flanking breaks the advantage.
Aegis converts successful Perfect Guards into a brief mobility-flow window for repositioning.
Meteor builds the highest straight-line Stampede peak but loses momentum rapidly when steering.
Ravager keeps more charge through moderate steering, trading Meteor's peak impact for flexible routes.
Fixes and Validation: Repaired the unused Cannon structural multiplier so v1.7 siege mechanics now interact correctly with destructible Battlefield cover.
Added ten Apex regression tests covering cadence, precision, brace recovery, sector geometry, blast commitment, structural pressure, anchoring, Perfect Guard flow, and ram identities.
Production build and the complete Node test suite pass before deployment.

releases.headline: Gunners master cadence, Cannons program space, and Guardians fight with facing.

Gunner — Fire Discipline: The cyan lineage gains deterministic recoil, weapon heat and a readable cadence window instead of flat hold-to-win sustained fire.
Stable aim and controlled bursts tighten fire; excessive heat increases predictable dispersion and physically pushes the hull backward.
Miniguns reward maintaining a sustainable mid-heat cadence while shotgun descendants reward bracing, recovery and deliberate re-engagement.
AI Gunners use the same heat/recoil model and deliberately vent after exceeding a sustainable firing state.
Cannon — Fire Control: The orange lineage can program detonation distance directly with right-stick depth while right-stick direction continues to aim normally.
A projected fuse/impact reticle shows the programmed burst point; desktop mouse distance follows the same interaction grammar.
Surviving Cannon projectiles airburst at the chosen distance while preserving their normal splash and cluster behavior, rewarding prediction and area placement rather than direct-hit aim alone.
Fuse placement compounds Battlefield cover and breach play because Cannon shells and splash can deliberately damage destructible barricades.
Guardian — Facing and Counterplay: The pink lineage gains directional frontal armor: aim direction now also determines the tank's strongest defensive facing.
BULWARK and IRON WILL become directional guard states instead of legacy 360-degree invulnerability or universal reduction.
The opening fraction of a second after a defensive activation is a Perfect Guard window. Reading an incoming attack correctly negates it and stores a Countercharge for the Guardian's next projectile.
Juggernaut, Meteor and Ravager build Stampede impact by maintaining a clean straight line; sharp turns and terrain collisions dump stored charge.
Readability and AI Parity: Cyan heat/cadence arcs, orange fuse markers and pink frontal-guard/charge visuals expose the new mechanics without adding buttons.
Procedural cadence, overheat, fuse-burst, Perfect Guard, Countershot and charge-break sounds reinforce important state changes.
AI uses the same heat, programmable-fuse authorization, directional defense and momentum constraints rather than receiving simplified privileged versions of the systems.

releases.headline: The arena becomes terrain: cover, lanes, line-of-sight and breachable ground.

Battlefield Geometry: Each run now uses one of three mirrored tactical battlefield layouts: Crossfire, Split Horizon, or Four Gates.
Permanent walls and pillars create real firing lanes, protected crossings, flank routes, choke points, side pockets and contested approaches without turning the arena into a maze.
Destructible barricades create temporary cover that can be cracked, breached and permanently converted into non-blocking rubble during the run.
Tank, AI, shape and powerup spawn placement is terrain-aware so entities do not materialize inside solid geometry.
Line of Sight and Projectile Physics: Solid terrain blocks automatic target acquisition and AI firing authorization; targets behind cover are not valid free aim-assist or AI shots.
Forward Observers also require unobstructed terrain line-of-sight before a remote sniper contact remains valid.
Projectile-to-terrain collision uses swept segment tests, so fast Rail and precision rounds cannot tunnel through thin walls between frames.
Permanent fortifications stop projectiles. Destructible cover absorbs projectile damage and splash, with shells dealing extra structural damage.
A high-penetration projectile may punch through a barricade only when that impact actually destroys it and the projectile retains enough penetration/integrity.
Movement, Drones and AI: Tanks, drones and neutral shapes physically collide with battlefield geometry and slide along it instead of ghosting through walls.
AI loses firing permission through occlusion and changes path/strafe intent after repeated terrain bumps instead of continuously pushing into a wall.

Controller drones remain terrain-constrained during farming, defense, formation and manual command. A committed drone dash that hits a wall aborts into recovery rather than dealing impossible through-wall damage.
Controller Command Nodes can still be placed tactically beyond cover, but the squad must physically reach the space rather than teleporting its threat through geometry.
Sniper and Observer Tactics: Cover can now break a sniper reconnaissance chain without killing the Observer: suspicion may guide the scout toward activity, but actual contact requires a clear cone and clear terrain sight.
Sniper hulls retain ordinary direct sight, so walls create genuine approach windows, relocation choices and Observer-positioning decisions.
The result is a real detect → acquire → line up → fire interaction layered on top of Silent Horizon and Violet Doctrine rather than simple long-range visibility.
Presentation and Validation: Fortifications use layered shadows, neon rim lighting, damage cracks, impact flashes and persistent rubble so collision geometry is visually explicit.
A compact battlefield strip names the current layout and reports remaining destructible cover without adding another control surface.
Added procedural cover impact, breach and terrain-scrape SFX with restrained particles/camera response.
Node regression tests cover Battlefield release wiring, line-of-sight blocking, swept thin-wall collision and terrain-aware spawn safety.

releases.headline: Blackglass is polished, drones coordinate properly, and reconnaissance learns to search.

Blackglass Polish: Portrait-mobile showroom layout was rebuilt for narrow phones with a horizontal dossier rail, shorter animated stage, safe text wrapping, aligned telemetry, and non-overlapping graft rows.
Long class-role labels truncate intentionally inside library cards while the selected dossier retains complete information.
Drone Discipline: Idle Controller drones use persistent steering plus separate return/resume thresholds instead of vibrating between farm and home decisions.
Friendly drones reserve different harvest shapes whenever alternatives exist.
Defensive drones automatically intercept nearby hostile combat drones; Forward Observer spotters are exempt from automatic defense.
Manually directed Controller swarms can attack any hostile drone, including spotters.
Forward Observer Intelligence: Observer search uses a roughly 700-unit, ~149-degree cone plus short point-blank awareness.

Recent contacts and nearby hostile projectile trajectories create decaying suspicion bearings that rotate the cone and bias patrol movement toward likely activity without granting magical unseen target coordinates.
Observers continue purposeful sector searches after losing contact and still harvest shapes encountered while scouting.
Player snipers receive clear cyan target relays and off-screen CONTACT markers with distance; hostile observer relays provide readable SPOTTED / OBSERVER information.
Music and Presentation: Added a distinct procedural NOVA lobby theme with a repeatable syncopated motif and neon bass pulse.
Opening Blackglass smoothly morphs the lobby score into a crystalline intelligence-room variation while respecting SOUND OFF, MUSIC OFF, and autoplay restrictions.
The precision SHOT edge callout now remains screen-upright.

releases.headline: The Evolution Tree becomes a living tank intelligence archive.

Tank Intelligence Showroom: The lobby lineage section expands in place into a complete 36-class dossier library.

Every tank gets lineage context, evolution breadcrumbs, a unique catchphrase, tactical description, ability information, runtime telemetry, and an animated preview generated from canonical class data.
Trait Graft Lab: Foreign lineage genes can be previewed on the selected build with exact base before → after changes to relevant weapon, hull, mobility, body, splash, drone, and reduction stats.

releases.headline: The full sniper doctrine belongs to every purple tank.

Purple Lineage: Marksman, Railgun, Ghost, Singularity, Prism Rail, Specter and Assassin all use Forward Observer authorization beyond ordinary direct sight.

Non-beam purple forms gained class-specific precision dwell, staged warning cues, suppression, projectile readability, and punishable post-shot reveal while Rail forms retained beam-specific focus/interception mechanics.
Observer Counterplay: Destroying the active Forward Observer temporarily disables remote relay while leaving normal direct-sight combat intact.

releases.headline: Snipers need eyes before they can kill beyond sight.

Sniper AI: Fixed banked AI Rail focus and replaced instant reacquisition with finite tracking, continuous focus, sampled target motion, and post-shot recovery.
Sniper hull sight is ordinary-range; distant target authorization comes from a destructible Forward Observer.
Safety: Evolution transitions clear hostile banked focus, collapse the upgrade tray, and grant a brief re-entry grace period.
Controller drone state receives invariant repair for broken positions, phases, targets, dash vectors, and Command Nodes.

releases.headline: Sniper and Controller mastery gets a full feedback pass.

Polish: Added segmented Rail focus feedback, enhanced projectile trails, RAIL DENIED, formation previews, swarm-state visualization, DIVE BROKEN / EVADED feedback, richer procedural SFX, and selective haptics.

Controller Combat: Right-stick direction commands swarm bearing, analog depth sets deployment distance, and release recalls the squad while the left stick continues moving the hull.
Controller PvP uses designation, formation geometry, readable wind-up, trajectory commitment, dive, overshoot and recovery instead of autonomous nearest-target ramming.

releases.headline: Snipers become lethal, readable skill duels.

Sniper Gameplay: Rail forms gained focus-to-fire, weaker quick-shots, aim commitment, off-screen directional warnings, suppression, post-shot reveal, explicit interception integrity, and swept projectile collision.

Drones: Introduced combat drones as persistent arena entities with health, targeting, respawning and combat behavior.
Controller builds gained hunter swarms as their defining combat identity.

Foundation: Initial playable release of NOVA TANKS.
